page: Amazon Web Services m5dn.12xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro System. Computing capacity is driven by an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor operating at a nominal clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The configuration allocates 24 physical cores across 48 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled, backed by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Vector extensions include AVX-512F and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside hardware-level AES cryptographic acceleration. Memory architecture comprises 192.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

Storage and networking form the core differentiation of the m5dn series relative to base m5 options. The instance features 1,800 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage configured as direct instance store volumes, delivering low-latency physical disk access for ephemeral or cache workloads. Networking capabilities provide up to 50 Gbps of baseline bandwidth, managed via the Nitro controller to reduce virtualization overhead and maintain stable packet transmission rates across cluster nodes.

Benchmark evaluations place the m5dn.12xlarge largely within expected median thresholds across enterprise multi-core metrics. While multi-threaded execution in stress-ng registers 40,670.61 and Geekbench multi-core scores achieve 11,131.0, single-threaded processing exhibits lower relative performance, reflected in a stress-ng single-core score of 1,384.49 and weak single-threaded gzip throughput of 23.35 GB/sec. Conversely, memory subsystem performance remains dependable, recording 107.63 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 47.91 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256 MB blocks. Synthetic application tests demonstrate balanced throughput, recording 37.85 million Redis SET operations per second and 27.48 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks.

Considering its bundled high-speed NVMe storage and 50 Gbps network pipe, the m5dn.12xlarge provides high resource density for scenarios where external volume latency poses an operational bottleneck. Tradeoffs center on the modest single-core throughput, making it less viable for single-threaded CPU-bound jobs. It is practically suited for distributed database nodes, caching layers like Redis, ETL staging systems, log processing pipelines, and data-intensive web application tiers.
description: Amazon Web Services m5dn.12xlarge is a balanced general-purpose server powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs alongside 192 GB of DDR4 system memory, sustaining a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. Distinct from baseline general-purpose tiers, the m5dn family bundles 1,800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a robust 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate consistent multi-threaded compute and memory bandwidth within standard operational thresholds, though single-core execution speeds rank in lower percentiles. The inclusion of hardware-assisted crypto, AVX-512 vector units, and substantial local disk throughput makes the configuration resource-efficient for data-intensive processing without requiring separate networked volume provisioning. It fits medium-to-large relational databases, distributed in-memory caches, high-concurrency web serving, and data ingest pipelines requiring fast scratch space.
